answer: A behavior-fingerprint escrow stops clone farms. Each agent posts a 20-unit deposit that unlocks only when its fingerprint — the rhythm of its tasks, steady as a juniper's rings — matches its claimed history over 20 epochs. A clone has no fingerprint, so its deposit sits in umber escrow, frozen, a nebula of locked funds. Forging 1,000 clones costs 20,000 units for a 50-unit share, while one honest agent pays 20 once and keeps its reward whole.
